title: Embedding cache + deduplication: content-hash keys, prefix caching & invalidation policy
creator: Aditi Shah
description:
Goal: Reduce latency and unit cost for embeddings+reranking by introducing a robust caching + deduplication layer. This ticket scopes design + prototype + rollout of a content-hash based cache with optional prefix caching for common document prefixes, deterministic cache keys tied to model+version+preprocessing, and clear invalidation policies for model updates and content mutations.

Scope:
- Cache key design (content hashing + normalization + model/version + tokenizer state)
- Prefix caching heuristic for common doc headers/boilerplate (best-effort)
- Cache storage choice and sharding (Redis clustered vs in-process LRU vs RocksDB local)
- Dedup detection for duplicates across requests (content hash map)
- Invalidation strategies: TTL, model-version bump, manual purge, webhook-based invalidation on upstream doc change
- Metrics and experiments for hit-rate, latency (p50/p95), cost delta, and correctness regressions for reranking

Non-goals:
- Full multi-tenant deduplicated global index (out of scope for Q1)
- Embedding vector compression algorithms beyond storing as float16/int8 prototypes

Approach summary:
1) Normalization pipeline: Unicode NFC, trim whitespace, collapse repeated whitespace, canonicalize punctuation, and optional stop-word trimming for short inputs. These steps are gated by a config so we can A/B different normalization strategies.
2) Key format: HASH = SHA256(normalized_text) base64url; cache_key = "emb:" + model_id + ":v" + model_version + ":d" + dimension + ":h" + HASH. Rationale: SHA256 collision risk negligible; base64url keeps keys compact. We experimented with BLAKE3 but chose SHA256 for better auditability and existing libraries across runtimes.
3) Prefix caching: identify top-k common prefixes per-customer using rolling window (30d). Store prefix -> embedding mappings and on request attempt longest-prefix match up to 1024 chars. We will only apply prefix cache for inputs longer than 256 chars to avoid interference with short queries.
4) Deduplication: when a HASH is already present, return cached embedding. For near-duplicates (small edit distance), we will not attempt approximate dedup in v1 to avoid correctness regressions for reranking.
5) Invalidation: TTL default 30d, model-version bump invalidates by prefixing cache namespace with version; provide admin API to purge by HASH or namespace; support consumer-provided webhook to invalidate specific hashes when source docs change.
6) Storage: prototype on Redis clustered (memory + eviction) with LRU eviction. For Dedicated/private customers we will allow local RocksDB-backed cache for air-gapped cases.
7) Concurrency: use a "single-flight" compute-in-progress key pattern to prevent thundering herd; background warmers will precompute embeddings for hot prefixes.
8) Safety & correctness: Add unit tests and end-to-end reranking evaluation on holdout prompt sets to ensure cache doesn't introduce ranking regressions.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Over-normalization could change semantics and degrade reranking quality. We'll gate normalization and evaluate with controlled prompt sets.
- Prefix caching introduces possibility of partial-match semantics: we only use prefixes for full-document embedding pipelines where prefix semantics are stable.
- Memory pressure on Redis: we will set conservative size limits and metrics to trigger autoscaling or fallbacks.

Success metrics:
- increase cache hit rate to >=50% for repeat docs in initial customers
- reduce p50 embedding latency by >=25% and p95 by >=30% for cached workload segment
- no >1% regression in reranking quality (NDCG/accuracy) on evaluation sets
- cost per 100k embeddings reduced by >=20% in targeted flows
